confirmed: The public cs_disasm_iter implementation is compiled in X86DisassemblerDecoder.c when x86 is enabled (production source lines 3732-3783). Changing the shared inline selector can therefore alter the public iterator, including its non-x86 paths.

In the Clang 18 PuTTY32 original consumer, R1360 executes 6144822 more host instructions in two traversals, including 5692416 in cs_disasm_iter and 452406 in X86_mayDecodeFeatureExtensionImpl. Reads and writes also increase. This establishes an execution-cost regression rather than attributing the entire timing loss to code placement.

R1361 leaves X86DisassemblerDecoder.c.o and the other 35 non-Mapping runtime objects byte-identical to production. PuTTY32 extra instructions drop to 5886 (Clang18) and 3924 (GCC11); ARM-detail and MIPS-format instruction, read and write totals exactly match production in both measured profiles.

Moving only the negative-filter table to a separate read-only section leaves executable object bytes identical and does not change the measured dynamic instruction/read/write totals relative to R1360.

The completed mixed native control changes only table placement, with every linked text symbol retaining its address and size. On GCC11, moving the 256-byte table out of the general read-only section restores the original ARM tables to their baseline addresses and improves ARM detail throughput by 19.4-19.6% relative to R1360 across ls/sort/cp. This isolates data layout as a cause of the earlier large ARM regression; no particular hardware cache mechanism has been proved.
unresolved: Callgrind cache and branch simulations are not hardware PMU evidence.

R1361 is held: the complete native gate has 3 below-0.99 observations, and the mixed gate has 26. PE32 formatting cost traces are running to distinguish extra execution from code-placement sensitivity.

R1361 leaves backend objects unchanged but shifts formatter and ARM/AArch64/MIPS code symbols forward by 80 bytes in all four mixed profiles. Their key constant-table addresses match production. This is an observed layout change, not yet a causal explanation for every remaining timing regression.
